interface.title: ParticleLens
interface.field: Microscopy image analysis: particle, droplet and emulsion sizing (materials science, colloids, pharmaceutics)
interface.stage_of_work: Measurement and quality control of acquired microscope images, through to exporting results for the analysis record
interface.what_it_is_for: Runs automatic circle detection on a microscope image in the browser. You set the physical scale, correct the detected circles by hand, check the size statistics and histogram, then export a CSV of diameters and an annotated PNG.

data.note: mixed-droplet-emulsion-1024.jpg (a synthetic brightfield emulsion with no scale bar) was loaded through the 'Open a microscope image' drop zone. Following the user guide, I set scale length 100 µm and 0.5 µm/px, sensitivity 0.75, diameter limits 4–180 µm and CLAHE. The first run found 128 particles in the main distribution (mean 15.66 µm, median 11.90 µm). Detection runs locally in the browser.

tree.general: Measure the size distribution of round objects in an image and save a corrected, documented result
tree.specific: Size the droplets in a microscope emulsion image, correct the detections and export a CSV plus an annotated PNG

features.name: Editable circle-annotation canvas with tool palette
features.general: Review automatically placed round markers on an image and correct them by hand: select one or several, drag to move, draw a new one by its diameter, delete, with zoom, pan and fit-to-view
features.specific: Image editing canvas with Select (V), Hand (H), Draw circle by diameter (C), Delete, zoom in/out, Fit view (F), and a toolbar you can dock left, right, top or bottom
steps: Click a circle to select it, or Shift-click to add more
Left-drag a selected circle to move it
Choose Draw circle and drag edge to edge across a missed object
Press Delete or the toolbar trash button to remove the selection
Zoom with the wheel, pan with Hand, press F to fit
serves_tasks: Move a misplaced marker
Add an object the detector missed
Remove false or unwanted detections
Navigate the image to inspect detections

features.name: Scale calibration: typed value or drawn reference line
features.general: Turn pixels into physical units either by typing a units-per-pixel value or by drawing a line over a reference of known length. A drawn line takes over and locks the typed value until you remove it, and all measurements update right away
features.specific: Scale length (µm) plus Length per pixel (µm/px), or Redraw scale bar (R) on the canvas; the header badge shows the source ('Direct input' or 'Scale bar'), and 'Remove drawn scale bar' unlocks the field. The README also describes automatic detection of a lower-right scale bar, which was not observed because the test image has none
steps: Type the scale length and µm/px, or
Press R and drag along a scale bar or known feature
Edit the scale length to recompute µm/px from the drawn bar
Press Remove drawn scale bar to go back to typed input
serves_tasks: Set the pixel-to-length calibration
Type the calibration directly
Calibrate by drawing a line of known length on the image
Change the known length of the drawn reference and recalibrate
Discard the drawn reference and go back to typed calibration

features.name: Scale and size-limit legend overlay
features.general: A floating legend on the image draws reference bars for the calibration length and the minimum and maximum object sizes, so you can judge size limits by eye before detection. It updates as you type and warns when a bar is too long to show
features.specific: 'Scale and diameter' panel showing Scale 100 µm = 200 px, Minimum 4 µm, Maximum 180 µm; toggled with 'Show scale legend on image' or its close button
steps: Change the scale or the min/max diameter
Watch the legend bars resize
Zoom out if it warns that a bar is too long to show
Hide it, or show it again with the checkbox
serves_tasks: Set the pixel-to-length calibration
Set detection parameters and run the detector

features.name: Tunable circle detector with explained parameters
features.general: Run a local shape detector with grouped settings (size limits, sensitivity, edge thresholds, contour acceptance, contrast preprocessing), each with an explanation popup, and re-run after changes; a status indicator shows whether the results match the current settings
features.specific: Particle detection panel: Advanced settings with Sensitivity, Min/Max diameter, Edge thresholds, Minimum edge support, Circle fit tolerance, Minimum contour coverage, and Contrast preprocessing (CLAHE, Background correction, None), then Run Detection; the status badge reads Loaded, Settings changed, Detecting or Detected
steps: Open Advanced settings
Read an (i) explanation and set the values
Choose a contrast preprocessing method
Press Run Detection and watch the status badge
Change settings and re-run to compare counts
serves_tasks: Set detection parameters and run the detector
Re-run detection with different preprocessing

features.name: Image display adjustments
features.general: Change brightness, contrast, gamma and colour/grayscale for viewing and export; a reset button returns the sliders to their defaults but leaves the colour mode as chosen
features.specific: Image adjustments sliders (Brightness, Manual contrast, Gamma), Preview and export color (Keep color / Grayscale), Reset adjustments (resets the three sliders only; Grayscale stays selected, screens/039.webp)
steps: Drag a slider
Choose Grayscale
Check the canvas
Press Reset adjustments to return the sliders to 0
Switch the colour back by hand if needed
serves_tasks: Adjust how the image is displayed

features.name: Linked measurement table and summary statistics with edge exclusion
features.general: A table of every measured object, linked to the image (clicking a row selects that object), with summary cards that update after each edit and leave out objects that are mostly cut off by the image edge
features.specific: Statistics cards (Main distribution count, Mean, Median, Range, Visible area ≥ 50%) and a Data points table (ID, Source Auto/Manual, X, Y, Radius, Diameter, Visible area) where excluded edge particles are greyed out
steps: Open Analysis and export
Click a row to select its particle on the canvas
Edit circles on the canvas and watch the counts and means update
Scroll to see Manual rows and greyed-out edge rows
serves_tasks: Read summary statistics and per-object measurements
Find a measured object from the table

features.name: Interactive size histogram with cumulative curve and live overlay
features.general: A histogram of object sizes with adjustable bin count, an optional cumulative-percentage line, hover read-outs, zoom, a mini version floating over the image that updates during editing, and image download
features.specific: Distribution tab: Bin count slider, Frequency/Cumulative/Live overlay toggles, Plotly chart (Pareto-style frequency plus cumulative line) with hover, box zoom and home, plus Download current chart (…_pareto.png); the floating 'Live distribution' panel sits on the canvas
steps: Open the Distribution tab
Drag Bin count
Turn the Frequency, Cumulative and Live overlay series on or off
Hover or zoom the chart
Press Download current chart

features.name: Configurable results export (CSV + annotated image)
features.general: Export the corrected per-object table and an annotated copy of the image. You choose which overlays go into the image (selection highlight, scale bar, legend), how many labels to draw, and a coloured margin; options that need missing data, such as the scale bar, stay disabled until it exists
features.specific: Export tab: Image label count, Image contents checkboxes (Selected particle highlight, Scale bar, Scale and diameter legend), Outer margin color/size, and CSV, Annotated Image or Export CSV + Image buttons
steps: Set Image label count (it also limits labels on the canvas)
Tick the overlays to include (Scale bar only after drawing one)
Set the margin colour and size
Press CSV, Annotated Image, or Export CSV + Image
